title: Transcriptional and epigenetic regulators of human CD8+ T cell function identified through orthogonal CRISPR screens
model: Primary human CD8+ T cells; dSaCas9-VP64 CRISPRa promoter-tiling library of 120 TFs and epigenetic regulators; TFome knockout library with BATF3 overexpression
contrast: CRISPRa: CCR7-high vs CCR7-low sort, paired by donor (3 vs 3). Second: TFome KO with BATF3 overexpression, IL7R-high vs IL7R-low (2 vs 2)
paper_method: DESeq2 per guide with NT-calibrated, p-weighted gene scores (CRISPRa); MAGeCK test, paired with NT controls (KO)
paper_calls: CRISPRa: 14 genes at adjusted p < 0.10, led by BATF, BATF3, EOMES (all CCR7-low); KO + BATF3: 276 IL7R-low genes at MAGeCK FDR 0.10, BATF3/JUNB/IRF4 named as cofactors
barcs_calls: CRISPRa: 2 genes at FDR 0.10 (BHLHE41, HIC1), 6 against the control null; KO + BATF3: 38 genes at FDR 0.10, 39 against the control null centred on the targeting guides
named_hits: Rank among all 120 genes by p (CRISPRa): BATF3 #57 (FDR 0.67), BATF #90, EOMES #34. KO + BATF3, rank among IL7R-high-depleted genes: BATF3 #12 (FDR 0.008), IRF4 #40 (FDR 0.15), JUNB #111 (FDR 0.35); IL7R #1
verdict: In the knockout screen BARCS tracks MAGeCK (Spearman 0.74) and calls BATF3, IL7R and the IL7R-high hits, but not the cofactors IRF4 and JUNB. In the CRISPRa screen its guide-level results match the paper's, yet its gene-level Stouffer sum dilutes the 2-3 active tiling guides of BATF3, BATF and EOMES, so none is called. BATF3 activation lowering CCR7 is the paper's own direction.
